en: So here in this project, I added one demo
skill, and of course you'll find that
attached.
I added it in a skills folder in my Codex
folder, and that is where you should add
your project-specific skills.
Alternatively, you could add a
.agents skills folder to your project and
put your skills there. Both works with
Codex. Why might this matter? Well, if you
are working with other coding agents, like
for example Cursor,
they also support this.agents
and therefore you would have one central
place to put your skills that can then be
leveraged by different coding agents. If
you're only using Codex, using that skills
folder is of course absolutely fine, but
that's something to be aware of.
Here, I'll delete it for now though.
Alternatively, you could go to your root
Codex folder in your user folder, and there
you'll have a skills folder too, and you
could add your skills here too. If you had
skills that should be shared across multiple
projects because they apply to every
project, which is not necessarily the case
for a Tailwind skill since not every project
may be using Tailwind. Tailwind is a library
that helps with styling web apps.
And therefore here I have a project-specific
skill in the skills folder and I have that
subfolder named modern-tailwind and in that
subfolder, the skill.md file. That skill.md
file then has metadata
where the name
has to match this folder name that is
required. That's the name of the skill.
And where I then have a description. And
this description is important because
the whole idea behind those skills is that
unlike AgentsMD, they're not loaded into
every session. Because as mentioned, you
could put all the extra information you know
matters for certain tasks. You could put
that all into AgentsMD. But of course, that
would mean that you load that whole pretty
big AgentsMD file
into the context window for every new
session you start. And all the content in
AgentsMD would be loaded in there, which
would include many instructions that may not
matter for the current task and which
therefore take up unnecessary space in the
context window. But maybe even worse,
you would load a lot of irrelevant context
into every session.
It's all about providing relevant context.
You will get worse results if you load a
bunch of information into every session that
doesn't matter for the specific task you're
going to execute there. So that's why
putting all your extra instructions and
knowledge into agents.md is not a good idea.
This file should stay lean and should only
include general knowledge and instructions
that apply to most or even all tasks. With
skills, it's different. Only the metadata is
loaded into every session. So if you have 10
skills, then 10 pieces of metadata are
loaded into the context window of every
session, nothing more. And it's then this
description that helps the AI agent decide
if it wants to learn more about a skill, if
it wants to load the rest of the content in
there.
That's why this description should give the
AI a clear hint about what the skill is
about. In my case, that is a skill that
helps it write clean, modern and concise
Tailwind code, and I clearly tell the AI
that this should be used whenever working on
or reviewing Tailwind CSS code. Because this
in the end is like a prompt, it's loaded
into every context window after all. And
then the agent should load the rest of this
skill if the AI decides that it's working on
a task where this skill is helpful. So it's
lazy loading the skill, so to say, it's only
loading it when needed.
